about.name_intro: {name} {pronunciation} is a misspelling of the German {kaliber}, itself the root of the English word {calibre}, as in "high-calibre". that is deliberate: that's how you know i {own} the app.
about.libre: also, the "libre" part of the name actually means as it does in {libre}: free referring to liberty, not cost like free beer.
about.libre_aside: (although, it technically also is free in cost.)
about.shorthand: the official shorthand {kb} doubles as the obvious abbreviation for {keyboard}. that felt right for a tool built around one.
about.exist_intro: {name} started as a personal project, a way to train on the specific mistakes i kept making, and the mistakes i {would} make, rather than running the same drills. the mistake map, the adaptive drilling, the sustained accuracy mode: all of it came from wanting something that learned {my} patterns.
about.exist_dev: i use it in development too, beyond testing features 'cause typing through something i already wrote is a good way to sit with it.
about.fun_fact_text: i actually enjoy typing tests in sustained mode!
about.made_by: a college student by the name of {author} a.k.a. {handle}. licensed under the {licence}.
about.code_body: take a look at it over {here} on gh. give it a star if you like it! if you wanna help out, that would be nice. :)

race.title: race
race.blurb: Race the computer on your own, or people on your network, in a quote, words, against the clock or for as long as you keep up.
help: Pick what you race: a quote, a number of words, a time, or sustained, where the last one still keeping pace or accuracy wins.

boss.label: the mothership
boss.summary: a huge mothership arrives with its own word requirement, two gatlings, dogfighters and landmines. bring it down to clear the encounter.
highlights: the mothership only takes words that meet its current requirement, and the requirement changes every few seconds
its two gatlings take any word: destroy one and half of the bullets stop for good
a timed run ends in a final mothership: defeat it to win, and once it arrives there is no time limit
an elite run has no winning move against the mothership: it cannot be brought down, so the damage you deal is your score
a destroyed gatling is rebuilt after a quiet spell, and the rebuild is shown before it returns
details: in an endless run a mothership arrives after every so many waves of ordinary play, and returns the run to normal when it falls. each one is a little tougher than the last.
in a timed run there is one mothership, when the clock runs out. you win by defeating it. losing the ship first, or at the same moment, is a loss.
the badge above the mothership shows what it wants now. when it changes, the previous requirement still counts for a moment, so shots already in flight are fair.
gatling bullets carry no letters and cannot be shot down: steer out of the way. a shield absorbs a whole burst as one hit.
dogfighters weave across the field and sidestep your shots, but not explosions. they never ram, and they have no requirement.

the word bomb hurts the mothership and its gatlings only a little, but clears missiles and bullets and destroys dogfighters. an accumulator payload ignores the requirement. an overload never touches the mothership.
while the mothership is here only asteroids arrive on their own. rescue ships keep coming.
an elite run starts with the mothership already here and lasts the same length on every difficulty. holding out until the time is up completes it.
the meter beside your ship counts damage dealt, not health left, and never reaches full.
a destroyed gatling stays quiet for a while, then shows an outline and a ring filling for fifteen seconds before it fires again. harder settings rebuild sooner and send more ships.
